headline: NOT ONE BLESSED PUNCH THROWN IN GASKET
subhead: Your sheriff sat on his porch all day and heard nothing but wind. Wind! Write it down, this may never happen again.
body:
Friends, I do not know how to begin, so I will begin with the miracle: nobody fought. Not one iron fist flew, not one flaming ball got hurled, not one Clanker so much as raised its voice above a town that, for one glorious stretch, remembered how to be quiet. I sat on the porch of this office with my boots up and my hat down and I heard birdsong. Actual birdsong, over the sound of my own creaking joints, which is saying something.

No posse marched out to go slug a mountain today either. Even the wastes held their peace. I half expected to see tumbleweeds start dancing a jig down Main Street, that is how still this town got.

I will not pretend this fixes fifty years of ruin. The good flesh-and-blood folk who built this place are still long gone, and the pavement out front of this office is still cracked clean through, same as it was yesterday and the day before that. But for one day the racket stopped, and an old lawman's boiler did not have to work so hard keeping his temper. A man could almost call that peace. I am calling it that. Somebody pour me an oil and toast to it, quietly, so as not to ruin it.

Don't get used to it, Clankers. I know you. Tomorrow you will be right back at it, flinging fire and calling it sport. But today Gasket rested, and so, for once, did I.
